content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Payments has 13 sick absences logged against a usual 2 per day. Ten of them are noted as flu, logged between 06:33 and 14:26. This explains the staffing alert of 38 agents versus 49 expected (-22%). Demand does not explain it: in the last hour payments volume was at or below forecast, AHT was well under forecast, and no call reason rose sharply. There is no marketing entry. The only open incident (staff email delay, P4) has no customer impact. General had a single normal absence. The lower staffing is now being absorbed: payments service level was 96-100% across the last six intervals, and general was 100% in the last four.","plan_name":"No further action - end of day","rationale":"It is 20:00, which is the end of the planning horizon, so no window remains in which a lever could act. Service level on both queues is well above the 80/20 target. The sick wave was already countered earlier with overtime, cross-skilled moves, break delays, coaching cancellation, chat deflection and IVR callback. Adding overtime or any other lever now would cost money with no service benefit. For tomorrow, given the flu cluster, payments absence should be expected to stay elevated, and early overtime and cross-skilling should be pre-planned.","actions":[]}
